Loki overview: 'A log stream is a set of logs which share the same labels.' Labels page: 'Each unique combination of labels comes in (for example, status_code="500") another new stream is created.'

Loki overview: 'Loki does not index the contents of the logs, but only indexes metadata about your logs as a set of labels for each log stream.' / 'Loki groups incoming logs into streams identified by a set of labels and indexes only that metadata.'

Loki v3.5.x log queries: 'All LogQL queries contain a log stream selector. Optionally, the log stream selector can be followed by a log pipeline.' 'Each expression is executed in left to right sequence for each log line.' Combined with the overview (only label metadata indexed) this supports 'selector answered from the index, pipeline reads the lines'.

Loki v3.5.x log queries, JSON parser: 'Nested properties are flattened into label keys using the `_` separator.' (example request.headers.Accept -> request_headers_Accept). Captured output loki-query.txt@stage-2 shows State_StatusCode >= 500 matching the 500 line, confirming State.StatusCode -> State_StatusCode.

Loki v3.5.x label filter: numeric types 'support the following comparators: == or = for equality, != ..., > and >= for greater than and greater than or equal ...'; string types work like Prometheus label matchers with =, !=, =~, !~. json-logs.txt@stage-2 shows State.Path "/api/v1/products/2" (string) and StatusCode 200 (number).

Loki v3.5.x query best practices: 'Loki creates one index file per day, so queries that span over multiple days fetches multiple index files. Lesson now uses the filtered query `{service="api"} | json | State_StatusCode >= 500` as round-1 suggested_text.

Loki labels page: 'High cardinality causes Loki to build a huge index and to flush thousands of tiny chunks to the object store.' 'High cardinality can lead to significant performance degradation.' Lesson now reads 'Loki's index then grows with every order, and Loki's performance degrades.' as round-1 suggested_text.
